人工智能现已成为华尔街最大的金融风险。纽约联储调查的市场专业人士中有87%提到了这一点，高于春季的50%。

items.excerpt:
Deal with Nevoya supports 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on I-10 between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona.
Artificial intelligence (AI) and social media giant Meta will purchase zero-emission trucking capacity from Nevoya, an electric truckload carrier, to offset the emissions of its business activities, the firms said Thursday.
Nevoya announced the multi-year agreement with Meta that support the deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. The deal includes bringing online electric trucking charging infrastructure with the 25 deployed trucks' charging matched 100% with renewable energy certificates.
According to Nevoya, Meta's purchase is not tied to the physical transport of Meta's own goods. Rather, companies purchase environmental attribute certificates (EACs) to address emissions associated with their value chains, including logistics. The agreement helps scale electric trucking in a region central to Meta's infrastructure, with the I-10 being a key route for moving data center construction materials across the southern United States.
"Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat. Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build," said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta.
This is Meta's second agreement with Nevoya. In Texas, Meta was one of several buyers in the Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers' alliance whose collective EAC purchases support Nevoya's 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor. This new Agreement is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta and gives Meta a framework to unlock additional corridors in the future. Nevoya expects the 25 I-10 trucks to begin operating in 2027 and to cover approximately 4 million freight miles annually.

items.excerpt:
Challenges include higher costs of doing business, due to tariffs, talent and wages, continued inflation, and raw material pricing.
Manufacturers have strong optimism for growth in 2027, but they have much less confidence in turning stronger demand into profits, according to an industry survey from Wipfli.
Specifically, two-thirds expect revenue growth, but only 25% are very confident in achieving 2027 profit goals, Milwaukee-based advisory and accounting firm Wipfli said in its “Manufacturing Pulse Survey.” As another measure of that balanced view, 52% are becoming more selective about the opportunities they pursue, signaling a greater focus on the quality of new business.
The Q4 2026 survey of 342 manufacturing facilities found overall sentiment has reached its highest level since 2022, supported by stronger growth expectations and improving business opportunities. Still, persistent costs, labor challenges, and pricing pressures are keeping profitability firmly in focus.
More specifically, higher costs of doing business remain manufacturers' leading concern, alongside talent and wages, continued inflation, and raw material pricing. Manufacturers also continue to navigate tariff impacts, with Section 232 affecting 71% of survey respondents.
Pricing remains another challenge. Just 29% of manufacturers reported successfully passing through most requested price increases in 2026, while 45% passed through some.
That combination makes operational discipline increasingly important as manufacturers prepare for growth. "Manufacturers have good reason to feel more confident going into 2027. We're seeing stronger demand, better quote activity and real opportunities for growth, but growth doesn't automatically translate into better profitability," said Laurie Harbour, partner, Wipfli.

Assent survey finds that 57% say incomplete data and data integrity are their greatest challenge in meeting compliance and sustainability reporting requirements.
Seven in ten manufacturers still rely on manual processes for compliance with accelerating regulatory and customer requirements, according to a survey from Assent Inc.
While manufacturers are highly engaged with product compliance and sustainability than ever, the survey found that their tools and data haven’t kept pace, Ontario-based manufacturing data network provider Assent said in its “2026 Product Compliance & Sustainability Trend Study.”
Three in four respondents (75%) said they are hands-on with those programs daily, yet 70% still rely on spreadsheets to manage product compliance, based on a survey of 131 manufacturing specialists conducted in partnership with Pforzheim University in Germany.
Respondents across automotive, electronics, and other industries report the same manual, reactive approach to compliance, with 57% pointing to incomplete data and data integrity as their greatest challenge in meeting compliance and sustainability reporting requirements. At the same time, artificial intelligence and automation rank as the single biggest opportunity they see ahead. Yet only 10% of respondents have actively incorporated AI into their processes.
That data gap is a risk that impacts the entire business. For example, emerging obligations such as Digital Product Passports and carbon reporting increasingly draw on the same supplier data. This information already feeds material compliance declarations, so a single weak supplier response creates risk in multiple domains at once. More than half (55%) of respondents in the survey cite data quality and timeliness as the reason supply chain carbon data doesn’t meet their standards.
“This research confirms what we hear from manufacturers every day: They know AI and automation are the next step for product compliance and sustainability, but incomplete data is holding them back. The path forward isn’t more point solutions; it’s a connected foundation of part, product, and supplier data that can be augmented with AI capabilities. Together, they empower teams to achieve compliance and sustainability goals,” said Catherine Cormier, Chief Innovation Officer at Assent.

items.excerpt:
Dario Amodei 在纽约 JPMorgan 活动上与 Jamie Dimon 对谈，对 Anthropic IPO 路演期间的市场动荡不以为意，称对上市时机和市场状况不太在意。
原文汇集了 IPO 规模、现金储备和算力采购策略等关键数字，有助于理解 Anthropic 上市背后的资金逻辑。
FT：在纽约举行的摩根大通活动上，Dario Amodei 与 Jamie Dimon 交谈时，对 Anthropic 路演期间的市场动荡不以为意。
摩根大通正在承销定于周四进行的纳斯达克上市，Amodei 对该行银行家表示，Anthropic 对上市时机或市场状况“并不特别在意”。
截至9月底，公司持有超过1300亿美元现金，而超额认购的发行加上一笔私募配售可能再增加1000亿美元或更多。
这笔缓冲资金为计划中的9000亿美元基础设施支出提供支持，其中包括每月价值高达31亿美元的SpaceX数据中心交易。
Dario Amodei：Anthropic 计划在算力上投入 9000 亿美元，但与竞争对手相比购买量“相对较少”
Dario Amodei 在 Anthropic 首次公开募股路演期间与摩根大通 CEO Jamie Dimon 进行的一场直播中发表上述言论。
Anthropic 只提前锁定规模适中、价格更低的算力，因此如果需求弱于预期，这样做是安全的。
如果需求强劲，它将在“现货市场”上购买额外容量，也就是按当前价格在短时间内租用可用算力，而不是预先做出巨额长期押注。
---- 来自“CNBC Television”YouTube 频道，（链接见评论）
Dario Amodei: Anthropic is set to spend $900B on compute, yet buys "relatively little" compared to rivals
Dario Amodei on a live-streamed with JPMorgan's CEO Jamie Dimon as part of Anthropic’s IPO roadshow.
Anthropic locks in only a modest, cheaper amount of computing power ahead of time, so it is safe if demand turns out weaker than expected.
If demand comes in strong, it will buy extra capacity on the "spot market", which means renting available compute on short notice at the going price, instead of making huge long-term bets upfront.

items.title: Jensen Huang 离任或给 AI 创业融资留下大缺口，投资人和创始人担忧
items.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 正式辞职，创投圈认为其继任者 Colette Kress 更保守，短期难延续他每年数十亿美元、今年已参与 105 轮的投资节奏。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kq4awkrys4uz37b7gsvj5r1dj
items.excerpt:
Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 正式辞职，创投圈认为其继任者 Colette Kress 更保守，短期难延续他每年数十亿美元、今年已参与 105 轮的投资节奏。
原文汇集多位投资人和创始人的判断，梳理 Jensen Huang 离任后 AI 创业公司融资可能出现的资本缺口和替代格局。
这是一则震惊全球的辞职消息。英伟达联合创始人、执掌公司33年的 深陷困境的CEO 黄仁勋 已正式卸任 。一位neocloud创始人向TechCrunch回忆起初闻此事时的感受：“就像炸弹爆炸了一样。”
过去几年，英伟达一直是活跃的投资者，每年向初创企业投入数百亿美元。据PitchBook数据，仅今年它就参与了105轮融资，且往往担任最大投资方。“如果这个方向发生变化，对许多年轻公司将是沉重打击，”Relational Capital创始人Maria Davidson表示。
投资者称，黄仁勋的离开让初创生态失去了最大的支持者之一，短期内资本也将大幅减少，这可能对交易撮合、估值、融资乃至竞争格局产生巨大影响。
“从应用层到neocloud，英伟达几乎支撑着每一家AI原生初创公司，”Dawn Capital的Shamilla Bankiya对TechCrunch表示。
Seligman Ventures管理合伙人Umesh Padval表示，投资初创公司的大多数重大决策往往出自黄仁勋本人。Padval自担任Mellanox Technologies董事时便与黄仁勋相识，这家网络芯片制造商于2020年被英伟达以约70亿美元收购。尽管有人希望黄仁勋的继任者最终能延续他的投资狂潮，但投资者并不看好这在短期内实现。
英伟达临时CEO Colette Kress 预计将推行一些调整 ，尤其是在英伟达对处于 数十亿美元数据中心建设 核心的AI初创公司的投资方面。黄仁勋在这一领域的大举投资一直令华尔街感到担忧。
“她保守得多，”一位投资者这样评价Kress，“我不认为她会投入同样多的资金来维持早期生态的运转。”
英伟达最大的押注集中在neocloud、推理服务提供商和开放权重模型上，这些领域对较小公司而言建设成本高昂。“正因如此，黄仁勋的举措是生态得以形成的重要原因，”硬件公司Ghost联合创始人Zain Javid表示。
例如，英伟达在CoreWeave仍为私有公司时便予以投资，并参与了Crusoe的两轮融资，包括其14亿美元的E轮。它今年以 130亿美元收购了Hugging Face （预计2027年完成交割），并持有Mistral AI、Lambda和Black Forest Labs的投资。英伟达在这些交易中往往都是最大投资方。据 《华尔街日报》 报道，去年在开源初创公司Reflection AI尚未取得可观收入之前，英伟达就在其20亿美元B轮融资中开出了8亿美元支票。
“黄仁勋相信开源，坦率地说，也相信欧洲，”Bankiya谈到黄仁勋为何在全球AI领域投入如此之多时表示。美国以外地区（如欧洲）失去这种支持，“将造成巨大的资金缺口，说实话也是生态缺口，没人能填补。”
同样不可否认的是，英伟达在生态中如此强势，有时让人感觉像垄断。通过以如此慷慨的支票支持众多公司，英伟达实际上将这些初创公司锁定在使用其芯片上，从而进一步巩固了其市场主导地位。
如果公司在初创企业投资上确实变得更加保守，那可能会给竞争对手和规模较小的玩家留下更多空间。（巧合的是，就在黄仁勋的英伟达风波之际，谷歌 本周发布了两款新芯片 。）
TechCrunch 采访的一些投资者希望，大型云厂商和其他芯片制造商能出手支持初创企业，填补黄仁勋很可能留下的部分空白。
例如，Battery Ventures 的普通合伙人 Dharmesh Thakker 预计，大型科技竞争对手将争夺英伟达的投资王冠，“这取决于谁能拿出最好的组合——出色的产品、生态与社区来与 CUDA 竞争，以及为生态提供资金支持的财力，”他说。CUDA 是英伟达的软件平台，让开发者能在其 GPU 上运行 AI 模型。
虽然谷歌、亚马逊、微软和 AMD 等公司可能会支持成熟初创企业，以推动自家芯片和云的采用，但 Thakker 怀疑它们会像英伟达那样，向尚无收入的基建初创企业投入数亿美元。
一位风投人士说，在黄仁勋治下，需要 1 亿至 5 亿美元 GPU 的基础设施公司，往往仅为了起步就能从英伟达那里以 10 亿美元或更高的估值拿到其中一半的资金。这家芯片制造商的参与，让其他投资者有底气以高估值支持这些公司。
如今，预计英伟达在支持新公司时会更加挑剔，同时对现有投资组合开出更小额的支票，这助推了估值下降。

At CoRL 2026 in Austin , GENTO showed humanoid robots and a new dexterous hand that sit on top of a stack Tianji Intelligence has been building since 2015, starting with a single component most people never see.
Most conversations about humanoid robots start with the AI model. Far fewer start with the torque sensor inside each joint, even though that part decides how a robot reacts when it pushes against something. For GENTO , that is exactly where the story begins.
GENTO , an independent humanoid robot brand incubated by Tianji Intelligence, develops humanoid robot systems, dexterous hands and teleoperation and data-collection platforms. Its humanoid systems incorporate Tianji Intelligence’s TIANJI-branded force-controlled arms.
At CoRL 2026, one result of that approach appeared on a bigger stage. A TIANJI Marvin Pro platform, built for NVIDIA by Tianji Intelligence, was used in demonstrations accompanying NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 launch on Nov. 9. GR00T 2 is an open world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos, and NVIDIA’s published research demonstrations show the platform assembling a toy truck and scooping granola with two hands.
A model like GR00T 2 needs a physical body to execute and evaluate what it has learned. Behind that body is a chain of components that starts inside each joint.
Tianji Intelligence was founded in Shenzhen in 2015 as an industrial robotics and motion-control company, incubated by Yaskawa Electric and Everwin Precision. In-house development of MEMS torque sensors began the same year. The company reports that these sensors offer 10 times the sensitivity of conventional strain-gauge designs without frequent recalibration.
When Tianji Intelligence moved into force-controlled humanoid arms in 2023 and 2024, it already had the sensing layer in house, along with four-loop closed-loop control and compliant impedance control, which regulates how a robot responds to contact.
The company describes its products as a five-tier stack, with each tier building on the one below. MEMS joint torque sensors handle perception. Integrated joint modules, which combine motor, reducer, driver, encoder and brake in one unit and weigh about 25% less than comparable modules, handle actuation. TIANJI dual arms come next, followed by GENTO whole-body systems and, at the top, the GENTO 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand.

Automated warehouses are changing how logistics work through intelligent material-handling systems, robotics and autonomous vehicles. However, increased automation in the workplace is introducing new safety challenges as machinery, moving equipment and people share the same complex environment.
The section below tries to highlight the importance of safety infrastructure in terms of protecting workers, preventing collisions and keeping warehouse operations running seamlessly.
Warehouse operations involve plenty of activities, from sorting inventory and receiving deliveries to packing goods, picking orders and preparing shipments. Demand for faster fulfilment has resulted in businesses turning to automation with the aim of managing repetitive, time-consuming tasks and enhancing accuracy.
Because of that, automated mobile robots (AMRs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs) and robotic picking tools can aid in transporting materials, moving goods and supporting inventory management with less manual handling. However, the introduction of these technologies comes with great change in how equipment and people operate in a workplace.
With effective warehouse safety infrastructure , companies can deal with the physical risks associated with a busy automated environment (where pedestrian and moving machinery routes meet).
Automation also plays an important role in improving workplace safety. This is done particularly by taking over tasks that expose employees to heavy lifting, frequent vehicle traffic and repetitive movements.
Machines can easily identify obstacles through cameras, sensors and collision-detection systems. On the other hand, automated processes can minimise unnecessary movement around the warehouse floor.
While these technologies are helpful, they don’t always eliminate every hazard. This means that a well-designed safety environment should combine physical protection measures with intelligent technology.

items.title: What Makes Modern Dentistry an Appealing Career Choice
items.description: Modern dentistry combines patient care, practical problem-solving, and opportunities to work with evolving technology. It offers several professional directions, from general practice to education and research, rather than one fixed career track. For anyone exploring a modern dentistry career, the appeal deserves a balanced look at both the opportunities and the commitment involved. Why does […]
items.excerpt:
Modern dentistry combines patient care, practical problem-solving, and opportunities to work with evolving technology. It offers several professional directions, from general practice to education and research, rather than one fixed career track.
For anyone exploring a modern dentistry career, the appeal deserves a balanced look at both the opportunities and the commitment involved.
Modern dentistry appeals to students who want to combine science, precise hands-on work, and meaningful interaction with people. Dentists need to evaluate evidence, solve problems, communicate clearly, and earn patients’ trust. That combination makes the profession worth exploring if you enjoy both analytical thinking and helping others directly.
The attraction is not simply working with teeth. Consider whether you would enjoy explaining a finding to someone who feels nervous, comparing treatment approaches, or concentrating on a small, technically demanding task. These are useful questions because compassion, communication, dexterity, and problem-solving all feature in the work.
When considering what makes modern dentistry an appealing career choice, start with those daily activities rather than the profession’s image. Prestige alone is a weak reason to commit to demanding training. Curiosity about the work itself gives you a stronger starting point.
Dentists diagnose and treat conditions affecting the teeth, gums, and related parts of the mouth. Their responsibilities also include advising patients about oral care and prevention. The profession therefore combines treatment with education: doing the clinical work is only part of the job.
For prospective students, that creates an important distinction. You should be interested not only in performing a procedure, but also in explaining why it matters and listening to the person receiving care. ADEA identifies compassion, ethical behavior, and the ability to earn trust as important qualities for future dentists.
During shadowing, pay attention to the conversations around treatment. Ask yourself whether you find the explanations, questions, and reassurance as interesting as the instruments. That reflection can help separate an interest in dental science from an interest in clinical practice.

items.excerpt:
Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
The Decoder 援引 WSJ 报道分析称，黄仁勋被罢免更多源于 Nvidia 高风险业务而非私生活传闻。Nvidia 在其主导下向 AI 云厂商和数据中心开发商提供数十亿美元财务担保以换取营收分成，最大一笔涉及对 OpenAI 俄亥俄数据中心的 2500 亿美元担保，消息公布后股价跌 5%，临时 CEO Colette Kress 将该承诺减半。
报道引 WSJ 细节梳理黄仁勋去职背后的担保信贷、客户集中等经营风险，可帮读者看清个人传闻之外的公司层面成因。
《华尔街日报》的一篇报道暗示，黄仁勋被排挤出局，更多是因为他的商业操作，而不是他的私生活。
据 《华尔街日报》 报道，黄仁勋在任期间，英伟达推出了一项高风险的信贷计划。公司向AI云服务商和数据中心开发商提供数十亿美元的财务担保，让它们买得起英伟达芯片。黄仁勋的女婿尼科·卡普雷兹（Nico Caprez）力推这项计划，并向合作伙伴承诺快速成交。作为回报，云服务商要把一部分收入分给英伟达。
最大的一笔交易是与OpenAI谈判，为俄亥俄州的一个数据中心提供2500亿美元担保。交易公开后，英伟达股价下跌5%。随后，此前担任CFO的临时CEO科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress） 把英伟达对OpenAI的承诺砍掉了一半 。缩减后的协议于8月签署。
据《华尔街日报》报道，克雷斯此前已在内部质疑这些担保如何估值、能带来什么回报，并试图约束卡普雷兹。据称在8月的一次会议上，黄仁勋称她“像一只被车灯照住的鹿”，还贬低她只是个“负责汇报的CFO”，在战略和决策上帮不上他。至少从去年起，英伟达及其他云和芯片公司的循环AI交易就 因吹大泡沫 而受到批评。
据报道，英伟达的股票估值也让黄仁勋不满。5月至10月间，公司月均市盈率从23倍降到16倍，英伟达的回应是启动了公司史上规模最大的股票回购。
大型云服务商当时正计划采用替代芯片，减少对英伟达的依赖。而英伟达已承诺采购大量晶圆和内存，黄仁勋把这一威胁形容为冲向这家芯片公司的“雪崩”。
在10月柏林GTC大会上，黄仁勋借一个日本汤店老板的故事向六位云服务商CEO施压。他说自己排了很长的队，喝到了人生中最好喝的汤之一。当他想要第二碗时，老板拒绝了，因为排队的人太多，汤也快卖完了。据《华尔街日报》报道，黄仁勋对CEO们说：“他比你们所有人都更懂做生意。”
这个故事的道理是，汤店老板没有把全部库存卖给一两个顾客。他保持高价，同时让客源保持广泛。黄仁勋说，云服务商没有照这个例子做，而是把过多算力卖给少数几个大客户，没有分散到众多买家手中。“你们没有在建立我产品的价值，”黄仁勋说。
黄仁勋究竟是眼看局面失控而主动离开（这似乎不太可能），还是董事会看到了借私生活问题施压的机会，目前尚无报道。
另外，据 CNN报道 ，涉及Alice Huang的间谍指控站不住脚。目前收集到的情报并不能证明她确实为北京从事间谍工作。即便在美国政府内部，对证据是否充分也存在分歧。

items.description: Newcomer 在旧金山 Cerebral Valley AI Summit 现场报道：Jensen Huang 因第二段婚外情披露辞职，Reuters 当天报道存在第三段，与会者多认为 Nvidia 短期无碍但生态承压，Databricks CEO 称其对整个生态是打击。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/p1mfh9oe0xbq4evyru5pp1ikt
items.excerpt:
Nvidia Crises, Anthropic IPO & Off-the-Charts Demand Have the AI World in a Tizzy
Newcomer 在旧金山 Cerebral Valley AI Summit 现场报道：Jensen Huang 因第二段婚外情披露辞职，Reuters 当天报道存在第三段，与会者多认为 Nvidia 短期无碍但生态承压，Databricks CEO 称其对整个生态是打击。
一线现场记录把 Nvidia 危机与 Anthropic IPO 放在同一画面，可直接看到行业领袖对生态冲击的即时判断。
AI 创始人和投资人周四齐聚旧金山，参加 Newcomer 举办的 Cerebral Valley AI 峰会 ，此时的新闻头条已经戏剧性到不能再戏剧化了。
黄仁勋 承认与一名疑似中国间谍有染后，他的命运悬而未决。这类丑闻有一条可靠的规律：一旦最初的新闻爆出，后面总会有更多料。周四上午果然如此——在第二段婚外情被曝光后，黄仁勋辞职了。
在 CVAI 的台上、走廊和各个角落，行业领袖们正在 实时研判 这对他们的公司以及 AI 经济这台庞然大物意味着什么。多数人认为，英伟达短期内不会有事，但之后会怎样谁也说不准。也许一个被削弱的英伟达有利于芯片竞争，但对开源未必是好事。最初的难以置信，逐渐变成了一个共识：英伟达董事会别无选择，只能让黄仁勋走人。
从四面八方涌来的 连环 爆料 拼出了一幅图景：黄仁勋讨好 特朗普总统 ，说服他无视情报界的警告——他情人担任高管的 Singapore 公司 Megaspeed，其实是北京设立的掩护机构，目的是规避美国的出口管制。 路透社 当天晚些时候报道，还有第三段婚外情。紧接着，关于英伟达内部运作方式的 猛料 也来了。
转眼之间，黄仁勋——这个全球最重要行业里最有权势的高管——的形象被 彻底重构 ：从无可匹敌的豪侠创业者，沦为无数 表情包笑话 的笑柄，成为 一长串 因傲慢而栽跟头的成功男士中的最新一位。CVAI 现场呈现出一种耐人寻味的双画面：与会者一边消化这桩劲爆新闻，一边惊叹于前方的 AI 机遇。
黄仁勋的倒台，距离 Anthropic 计划中的 IPO——或许是史上影响最重大的 IPO——只有几天，距离一场显示出公众对 AI 深度反对的选举也才一周多，这真是戏上加戏。周四许多演讲者表示，这样一位备受敬仰的人物竟跌落得如此之惨，令人难过；同时他们也相信，至少短期内英伟达会挺过去。
在 X 上，黄仁勋收获了 一片声援 ，其中包括 埃隆·马斯克 和 Garry Tan ，他们对一位英雄创始人被赶下台感到愤慨。 阴谋论 ——说这一切都是为了扼杀开源 AI 的心理战，或是针对特朗普的阴谋——在互联网上蔓延开来。在一些辩护者看来，黄仁勋唯一的错误就是没能拿到公司的投票控制权。
更有思考的声音承认，这场风波暴露了创始人崇拜的危险：它让所有人都对事后看来明显可疑的行为视而不见。很可能，最糟糕的还没爆出来。
General Catalyst CEO Hemant Taneja 不得不在 CVAI 第一个登台，他处境尴尬，却称赞英伟达董事会“做了件难事，履行了受托责任”。他谨慎地提出，一个被削弱的英伟达可能给 AI 芯片带来更多竞争，这或许是好事。事实上，本次活动的一大主题，正是要确保智能的获取不被少数大公司控制。
不过，并没有多少人真正在庆祝。Databricks 的 Ali Ghodsi 在台上谈到英伟达的危机时说：“这对所有东西、所有玩家都是打击，除了他们的直接竞争对手。这对整个生态是坏事，对新云厂商是坏事，对所有人都是坏事。他们曾是整个生态的支柱。”
当天早些时候， Shaun Maguire 提出 由 Palo Alto Networks 首席执行官 Nikesh Arora 作为执掌英伟达的候选人。在台上，Arora 回避了自己是否会接任的问题，但认同黄仁勋的离开可能带来一些短期动荡。 与黄仁勋关系尤为密切的高管，包括 Flapping Airplanes 总裁 Asher Spector 和 Perplexity 首席执行官 Aravind Srinivas ，都避开了这对各自公司可能意味着什么的问题；黄仁勋曾亲自领导公司备受争议的向客户投资战略，而这一战略很可能会被临时首席执行官 Colette Kress 收紧。
不过，多位发言者指出，尽管英伟达危机可能带来种种混乱，AI 的进展仍在加速。算力需求依然高得惊人。科技股因英伟达的消息一度受挫，但到周末已基本 企稳 。旧金山这座城市正焕发出久违的活力：过去五年我们在市中心待了很多时间，而周四是我们第一次觉得这座城市真的、彻底地回来了。
我们最喜欢的数据点之一，足以说明此刻的非同寻常：在我们与 Bessemer 共同打造的新 AI 100 顶级私营科技公司榜单上，AI 初创公司的估值中位数为 93 亿美元。这几乎是 Bessemer 一年前 Cloud 100 榜单上数字的两倍。
我们很可能仍处在英伟达丑闻的早期，而非尾声。联邦检察官、原告律师，以及新获权力的国会民主党人都在伺机而动。媒体正大快朵颐。电影人也不会落后太久。
如今智能体编程已证明其非凡价值，业内许多公司都在专注于降低成本。在短暂盛行的“堆 token”风潮之后，构成 AI 行业大部分收入的企业计算客户正意识到，成本可能很快就会变得非常高昂。专用芯片、开源大语言模型以及各种优化策略都在被采用。
围绕开源大语言模型的争论正变得更加激烈。行业内部出现了真正的分歧：一方认为智能最终将成为一种商品，主要由开源模型驱动；另一方则认为前沿实验室能够保持决定性优势。
初创公司担心未来 Anthropic、OpenAI 和大型科技巨头会有效控制对前沿智能的访问。
眼下所有热度都集中在基础设施上，背后的基本假设是终端需求在可预见的未来会持续纵向增长。然而在 CVAI 上，关于应用的讨论却出奇地少。编程是一个杀手级应用，但再往后就说不清了

items.title: 研究报告称中国最强 AI 模型使用了被禁出口的 Nvidia Blackwell 芯片训练
items.description: Will DePue 领导的非营利研究组织 Unemployment Labs 分析 DeepSeek、月之暗面、MiniMax 和蚂蚁集团开源模型权重，发现 Kimi K3 与 DeepSeek V4 等最受关注模型带有 Blackwell 芯片训练痕迹。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/q92ir58jcjtp3g9fn11jlb6ei
items.excerpt:
Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
Will DePue 领导的非营利研究组织 Unemployment Labs 分析 DeepSeek 、 月之暗面 、 MiniMax 和蚂蚁集团开源模型权重，发现 Kimi K3 与 DeepSeek V4 等最受关注模型带有 Blackwell 芯片训练痕迹。
研究称 DeepSeek、Kimi 等中国开源模型权重带有 Blackwell 芯片训练痕迹，文章还梳理了走私渠道与马来西亚离岸算力路径。
一项新研究称，中国企业开发的主要开放权重模型，是用美国政府禁止向其最大地缘政治对手出口的英伟达芯片训练出来的。
中国前沿实验室显然能广泛获取 Blackwell GPU，这说明这家领先的芯片设计公司面临的问题有多严重。英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋本周离开公司，此前他承认与 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 有婚外情，而 Megaspeed 是一家涉嫌向中国走私英伟达芯片的公司。Alice Huang 还被指是中国情报机构的特工。
尽管黄仁勋与一名客户和两名员工的关系最受公众关注，但英伟达因违反出口管制而可能承担的企业责任，很可能也是其决定与黄仁勋分道扬镳的因素之一。
美国的出口管制旨在保护其在 AI 能力上对中国的领先地位，但黄仁勋长期以来一直想打开这个市场。Blackwell GPU 被禁止出口到中国或中资企业，而特朗普政府允许英伟达出口性能较弱的 H200 芯片，条件是货物要走迂回航线，以便美国能征收 25% 的关税。
前 OpenAI 研究员、非营利研究组织 Unemployment Labs 负责人 Will DePue 分析了权重 ——即 DeepSeek、Moonshot AI、MiniMax 和蚂蚁集团公开发布的大语言模型的独特结构。权重仍能反映训练所用芯片的配置，DePue 找到了有力证据，表明最受关注的模型，包括 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 系列和 DeepSeek 的 V4 模型，都带有在 Blackwell 芯片上训练留下的指纹。
白宫技术顾问 Michael Kratsios 今年早些时候 表示 ，根据美国情报来源，Moonshot 使用了被出口禁令限制的英伟达芯片。非营利研究组织 Epoch AI 估计，2024 年和 2025 年约有 200 万枚先进芯片 通过 旨在隐藏最终目的地的各种手段进入中国。
这并不意味着这些模型完全是用英伟达芯片训练的，也不一定意味着违反了出口管制法；这些芯片可能位于境外数据中心，这已被证明是中国企业获取算力的常用方式，并 在马来西亚掀起了一场产业革命 。Epoch 的数据估计，2024 年和 2025 年有 27.5 万枚英伟达 AI 加速器进口到马来西亚。
然而，出口禁令的表面目标正是防止这种情况：中国 AI 实验室用最强芯片训练模型。对华鹰派长期以来一直呼吁加强对芯片使用者的管控，而不只是管控芯片所有者或安装地点。
“如果我们关心美国的技术优势，那么在我看来，不允许中国公司在中国大陆、香港和澳门获取芯片，却又说，其实你只要去马来西亚，就可以为所欲为，这完全说不通，”乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心研究员 Sam Bresnick 今年夏天对 TechCrunch 表示。
多年来，由Alice Huang执掌的Megaspeed一直通过其子公司Speedmatrix处于这类交易的中心，并先后受到美国政府和 新加坡 政府的调查。周五，彭博社 还报道称 ，一家与Alice Huang有关联的公司参与了向上海某数据中心走私被禁的英伟达芯片。
今年5月，做空研究机构Culper发布报告，认为英伟达存在“ 中国问题 ”，因为其收入的很大一部分由中国需求驱动，渠道要么是远程数据中心，要么是违反美国法律的走私。报告详细梳理了Megaspeed与英伟达的关系，并指称Alice Huang旗下公司背后有被禁止获取美国芯片的中国企业支持。
讽刺的是，做空机构Culper押注英伟达下跌，并非因为预期美国政府会出手打击。它真正关注的是中国政府对禁令的回应——重新全力投入本土芯片产业。
如果中国成功，中国对英伟达芯片的数十亿美元需求可能会枯竭。据报道，约有60万颗H200芯片 囤积在香港 ，等待运往中国。中国企业或许想要这些芯片，但对于它们为何迟迟未获进口许可，观察人士尚无共识。
斯坦福大学研究美中技术政策的研究学者Graham Webster表示，他不认同扣住芯片就能推动本土生产的说法，因为芯片需求实在太大。关于迟迟不放行的其他猜测包括：为一项可能涉及大量进口美国商品的贸易协议做准备，或担心芯片中可能藏有监控技术。
目前，美国企业在追踪客户如何使用AI芯片等受管制商品方面义务有限。但如果政府调查人员证实芯片走私确实发生、且黄仁勋知情，那么黄仁勋与Alice Huang在私人及商业上的牵连将给英伟达带来大得多的麻烦。英伟达和黄仁勋都为Megaspeed的数据中心做过担保，称英伟达官员曾实地走访，确认其合法合规。
美国政府对待英伟达和Megaspeed的方式也受到审视。负责监管芯片出口许可机构的商务部长Howard Lutnick，据报道可能丢掉职位，此前有报道称其调查人员 未能发现 可疑的芯片买家，且与英伟达官员 过从甚密 。

Eleven days later, DHL Supply […] The post Walmart’s $6 Billion Automation Bet and DHL’s Orchestration Strategy: Two Playbooks, One Hard Question appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Two announcements in the past three weeks sum up where warehouse automation stands at the end of 2026. On October 29, Walmart and Symbotic expanded their commercial agreement to bring more automation to 25 U.S. regional distribution centers, with an initial commitment of roughly $6 billion spread over several years. Eleven days later, DHL Supply Chain described a very different path: it is scaling the robots it already runs, moving AI orchestration into live warehouses, and piloting what it calls adaptive robotics.
Both are spending heavily, but betting on different ideas about what makes automation pay. For most operators, who are neither Walmart nor DHL, the difference between those ideas matters more than the size of either announcement.
Playbook One: One Vendor, One System, Network Scale
Walmart’s approach is consolidation. Symbotic now supplies a full system rather than a single product: high-density case storage, BreakPack for picking individual items, and SymMicro for store-based e-commerce fulfillment, all run by Symbotic’s own software. Walmart says the expansion will support e-commerce inventory upstream, add storage capacity and make replenishment more reliable.
When one company owns the storage structure, the robots and the control software, there are fewer handoffs between systems from different vendors, and fewer places for goods to pile up when one system cannot see what another is doing. The track record also lends weight. Symbotic reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $721 million, up 22% year over year, with 56 systems operating and 77 in deployment. Symbotic reported in August that deployment of BreakPack had begun at half of Walmart’s regional distribution centers.
Still, this is a commitment, not a result, and key pieces are still being proven. The first next-generation SymMicro unit was expected to take about six months to install at a Walmart store, and a possible order for 400 back-of-store systems depends on validating that second version. Symbotic itself has said its next revenue and margin inflection is expected in the second half of fiscal 2027.
DHL Supply Chain is betting on coordination rather than consolidation. The company says it has deployed more than 9,000 robots, completed more than 1.5 billion robotic picks and unloaded more than 10 million cases using Boston Dynamics’ Stretch robot. items.description: FlexLink’s RC20 collaborative palletizer has robotic safety features and a compact design to protect operators while maintaining throughput. The post FlexLink designs robotic palletizer to balance safety and throughput appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Floor space is at a premium in manufacturing facilities, and OEMs are being asked to fit more equipment into smaller spaces. FlexLink is addressing that challenge with robotic palletizing cells designed to protect operators without sacrificing production throughput.
The Gothenburg, Sweden-based company is part of Coesia . It designed its new RC20 collaborative palletizer for end-of-line operations and uses a FANUC CRX-20iA/L robotic arm, but its safety design extends beyond the robot itself. A detachable end-of-arm safety shroud, contact-sensitive padding, and integrated safety controls provide additional protection without requiring conventional barriers around the cell.
At PACK EXPO International 2026 in Chicago, David Shaw, FlexLink’s head of engineering for North America, explained why designing a safe palletizing cell requires more than selecting a collaborative robot .
“Safety is easy to get wrong on collaborative robotic cells. I always say there’s no such thing as a collaborative robot,” said Shaw. “It’s the cell that is collaborative, and that’s always something that’s definitely got to keep in mind with these things.”
FlexLink demonstrates the RC20 collaborative palletizer moving boxes through an end-of-line packaging application at PACK EXPO 2026. The robotic cell combines a compact design with integrated safety features to protect operators while maintaining throughput. Source: Sarah Wynn. Audio: Adobe Express
FlexLink designed the RC20 to operate without some of the protective equipment commonly used around industrial robots .
“In packaging, particularly for our end users, the real estate available in factories is at a premium these days. We’re trying to get more and more equipment in a smaller and smaller space,” said Shaw. “Being compact is one of our key parameters to work in.”
Shaw said the system does not require laser scanners, area scanners, or light curtains that may be needed for other robotic applications. This allows operators to move near the palletizing cell without routinely interrupting production.
“People can walk in and around the cell very easily,” he said. “We don’t inhibit production. We don’t inhibit throughput.”

items.title: GXO to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids from Apptronik in the next four years
items.description: Under the agreement, GXO and Apptronik will expand joint trials of Apollo in live operations across a range of warehouse workflows. The post GXO to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids from Apptronik in the next four years appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
GXO Logistics Inc. this week said it will expand its partnership with Apptronik. The company signed a letter of intent to expand development of Apptronik technology for deployment at scale.
The partners are working toward global rollout of up to 1,000 Apollo humanoid robots over the next four years. This is subject to the success of the deployments and the ability to meet agreed-upon performance, safety, and operational key performance indicators (KPIs).
“Humanoid robots are the latest evolution of intelligent automation, and their increasing dexterity will make them one of the most transformative applications of physical AI in logistics,” stated GXO CEO Patrick Kelleher. “GXO has deep experience turning advanced automation into operational value at scale. Our expanded work with Apptronik builds on that expertise as we identify and scale the applications where humanoids can deliver the greatest impact for our customers and team members.”
Under the agreement, Apptronik said that it and GXO will expand joint trials of Apollo in live operations across a range of warehouse workflows. These include goods-to-person ( G2P ) and person-to-goods picking , case and tote movement, packing , and sortation , according to the company .
“We started working with GXO in 2024, and through our partnership, we’re defining what it takes to put humanoid robots to work in logistics — measured against real operational KPIs in live facilities and delivering real value,” said Jeff Cardenas, co-founder and CEO of Apptronik.
“GXO has the network and the operating discipline to take this technology to real scale, across one of the largest logistics footprints in the world,” he added. “Our expanded partnership with GXO shows what’s possible when you pair a leading logistics provider with robots designed from the start for thoughtful collaboration with people.”
Beginning in 2027, the trials will validate the safety , security, and technical requirements for scaled deployment. The companies will assess and sequence each use case against jointly agreed productivity, safety and operational KPIs. GXO and Apptronik also aim to demonstrate how humanoids can work alongside existing automation and GXO team members.
Initial deployments are planned for North America in late 2027. The commercial framework is expected to follow a robotics-as-a-service ( RaaS ) model. This will allow GXO to scale humanoid deployment through a flexible, service-based offering.

items.excerpt:
Truly useful AI assistants need to be able to help users who ask misguided questions—not just users who ask the right question with the right amount of detail. We’re releasing XYBench , a benchmark of 8K+ questions that tests how AI assistants respond to requests based on misconceptions, such as asking how to thicken frosting that keeps sliding off cupcakes when the real problem is that the cupcakes are still too warm to frost. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at EMNLP 2026.
A mismatch between the approach someone asks about and the goal they want to achieve is known as the XY problem : a person wants to accomplish X, assumes a particular approach Y will work, and asks for help with Y. In the cupcake example, the person is so committed to making the frosting stick that they fail to consider the warmth of the cupcake as the true problem to be addressed.
Developed with researchers at Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins, XYBench exposes a critical gap in LLMs' ability to troubleshoot problems: recognizing when a user's request is based on an implicit misconception and appropriately redirecting them toward a solution that addresses their actual goal. Drawing on 8,115 real-world questions spanning programming and everyday activities such as cooking and home repair, we introduce a benchmark that measures whether models identify these misconceptions and are able to prioritize effective solutions in their responses.
The models we evaluated on XYBench – Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro – often suggested a solution to the user’s problem but kept their answers focused on the original, mistaken approach. Unlike human reference answers, all five models were less likely to steer users away from that approach and toward a solution suited to their goal.
People use AI systems with different levels of knowledge and may not always know how best to approach a problem. 个人智能体协议 （Personal Agent Protocol，简称 Poppy）自我们上月与首批设计合作伙伴 Meta、Genesys、Instinct、NiCE、Rocket、Shopify、Stripe 和 Walmart 共同发布这一新标准以来，已经获得了实实在在的进展。Poppy 让个人智能体能够通过企业智能体、网站和 API 与企业互动。今天我们很高兴地宣布：
Poppy 1.0 版体现了设计合作伙伴过去五周在真实网站、API 和智能体上测试草案所积累的经验。
该协议定义了个人智能体如何与实施它的企业建立连接，让智能体能够清晰、全面地访问企业提供的各项服务，其构建主要基于 MCP、OpenAPI 和 UCP 等现有标准。通过 OAuth 进行身份验证，客户可以控制个人智能体能做什么、不能做什么，并可以随时管理这些权限。
借助 v1.0，任何企业都可以自行实施 Poppy，并立即为使用 Muse 的客户带来更好的体验。我们的 实施工具包 会引导你完成设置，并附带一个验证器来检查你的工作。
Shopify 为 175 多个国家的企业提供服务，每个 Shopify 商店默认支持通用商务协议（UCP）。随着越来越多的购物行为转向个人智能体，现在每个 Shopify 商店都会自动发布 Poppy 文件，商家无需做任何额外实施。
UCP 与 Poppy 相辅相成。UCP 负责购物本身，比如查找商品、加入购物车和结账；Poppy 则负责在此之前发生的事：当智能体来到商店时，表明自己的身份，并了解自己可以做什么。
Shopify 联合编写了 Poppy 的商务扩展，把这两个协议连接起来。它让智能体既能以访客身份购物，也能用客户账号登录；在执行某些操作前，它会要求智能体先征询客户意见，因此智能体只在获得客户许可后才行动。它还能接入 UCP Ask，让购物者的智能体直接与商店的智能体对话。
我们非常感谢所有为这一新标准做出贡献的公司，也期待欢迎更多企业加入我们的设计合作。随着个人智能体承担越来越多日常事务，企业需要清晰、安全的方式与它们协作，同时继续提供值得信赖的体验。Poppy 为他们提供了这一基础——让企业与个人智能体能够为他们共同的客户把事情办好。
Mercury 不是银行。银行服务通过 Mercury 的 FDIC 保险合作银行提供。

This story originally appeared in the November 2026 edition of Logistics Management .
For decades, transportation managers have asked their systems to tell them where their freight was. They usually got their answer, but only after some sleuthing, a few phone calls to carriers and waiting while someone on the other end tracked it down.
Innovations like GPS, telematics and real-time transportation platforms sped up the process, and Amazon was raising the bar by making fast, trackable deliveries an everyday expectation. Around the same time, transportation platforms began generating little dots on the map that let shippers watch their freight make its way from Point A to Point B.
Fast-forward to today and we’ve reached a point where “knowing” where your freight is just isn’t enough anymore. Shippers also expect their systems to flag problems earlier, prioritize problem solving and handle previously manual tasks like carrier follow-ups and delivery schedule adjustments.
Toss artificial intelligence (AI), more precise analytics and automation into the mix, and you get a recipe for a more active freight management approach that goes well beyond basic visibility .
“Visibility in and of itself is just a means to an end, because you need visibility to start taking actions,” says Nathan Lease, senior director, logistics technology research and advisory at Gartner . “But just knowing that the truck is going to be late doesn’t do anything. The real question is: Can you act on that information?”
So, instead of tracking “where’s my truck?” companies now want to know “where’s my stuff?” “They want product SKU -level details of what’s on that container , what’s on that trailer and what the upstream and downstream implications of that visibility data are,” Lease explains. “Then, they’re using that information to make decisions about production planning, customer impacts and other operations.”
And that’s just one example of how freight management is changing. Technology, automation and AI now support everything from procurement and carrier management to routing and planning, while autonomous trucks are getting closer to reality. Earlier this year, Rhoda AI emerged from 18 months of stealth with $450 million in Series A funding. The company is working with customers in automotive, manufacturing, logistics, and e-commerce to deploy its direct video action, or DVA, model for robotics.
“We’re focused on deploying in the real world, and that means you have to deal with the messiness of the real world. Every run can be different,” Jagdeep Singh, the co-founder and CEO of Rhoda AI, told The Robot Report . “Every configuration can be different, and you need a really robust model. To build a robust model, you need a massive training dataset.”
A large training dataset is exactly what allowed large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT to rapidly progress in recent years. Physical AI has trailed behind those models because the same dataset doesn’t exist for the physical world, noted Singh.
“Every word ever put on the internet, from Shakespeare to Reddit, was used to train these AI models. Rhoda AI is betting on using video to data to close this gap and to create truly generalized robotics.

items.excerpt:
Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
Nvidia 前CEO黄仁勋辞职后，以色列科技界关注这家在其拥有6000名员工和最大海外研发中心的公司是否会继续深耕以色列。多位以色列投资人认为，Nvidia 决策放缓可能给 AI 芯片和推理软件领域的竞争者留出空间，但如果不确定性也拖慢 AI 支出，竞争者面对的可能是更小的市场机会。
文章从以色列视角梳理 Nvidia 领导层变动后的产业影响，投资人观点提示竞争者可能获得的窗口及其局限。
英伟达前CEO黄仁勋的辞职在以色列引发了 担忧 ，以色列被黄仁勋在2023年 称为 公司的“第二故乡”。这家公司的重要性是双向的，近年来这家半导体巨头为以色列的经济预测提供了 重大推动 。
英特尔、微软以及许多本土初创企业也在以色列开展相当比例的研发工作。但鉴于英伟达凭借其GPU在训练和使用大语言模型中的核心地位而在AI领域占据强势地位，以色列国内许多人都在猜测，这场领导层危机会引发多大程度的重新洗牌。
一如英伟达的诸多决策，黄仁勋推动公司在2019年 以69亿美元收购 了以色列芯片制造商Mellanox，并将该公司作为其在美国以外最大研发基地的基础。英伟达还 计划在以色列北部建造 一座耗资数十亿美元的园区。
以色列连续创业者、网络安全企业家Pavel Gurvich对TechCrunch表示：“黄仁勋通过收购Mellanox把英伟达带到了以色列，因此以色列科技界对英伟达和黄仁勋抱有强烈的正面情感。”
除了英伟达雇用的6000名当地员工之外，更大的问题是：在其他人掌舵的情况下，公司是否仍会像现在这样坚定地投入以色列。因此，那些希望公司延续这一承诺的人，和那些不希望此事发生的人，都在同样密切地关注着他的继任安排。
后者已经意识到，他们可能要失望了。在一段目前正在X上流传的2023年采访中，临时CEO Colette Kress曾 表示 ，作为英伟达CFO，她通常一天的工作“从以色列的会议开始，然后才继续处理加州的事务”。
Kress可能不会长期掌舵，但被提及接任这一职位的众多人选中 包括两位以色列人 ——苹果的Johny Srouji和英伟达的Michael Kagan——不过他们并不在 这份仍相当初步的名单 的最前列。
无论最终选中谁，黄仁勋的继任者对英伟达乃至整个科技行业的掌控力很可能都不及他。但投资者并不认为这会导致市场对英伟达产品的需求消退。
据Vertex Ventures Israel普通合伙人Yanai Oron的说法，“英伟达决策变慢可能会给竞争对手打开缺口，但如果这种不确定性也拖慢了AI支出，他们最终可能在一个更小的机会中占据更大的份额。”
英伟达在全球AI产业支出中占据了相当大的比重。在黄仁勋的领导下，公司动用现金储备在多个领域大举投资，既 投资企业 ，也投入自身的 下一代芯片 研发。
这样的帝国未必会随着其缔造者的离场而崩塌，但它成为完全垄断者的可能性似乎确实降低了。据Selah Ventures创始人兼管理合伙人Adi Levanon表示，“（黄仁勋的）离开不会瓦解英伟达的技术或生态，但可能给竞争对手更多空间去塑造接下来的格局。”
如今，全球企业正在将要求越来越高的AI智能体部署到工作流程中，大量关注——以及部分风险投资——正涌向 AI专用芯片 和 推理软件 的开发者，这些产品有可能与英伟达展开竞争。

items.excerpt:
When a distribution center begins to run out of capacity, the conversation usually turns to physical expansion. The company may need another building, a larger yard, additional dock doors, more equipment, or a second site closer to customers. Those are familiar decisions, supported by familiar metrics: square footage, pallet positions, average volume, and the cost of carrying another lease.
There is a question that should come before the capital request. Is the network actually short of physical capacity, or is too much of the capacity it already owns being lost between activities? A dock door waiting for a late trailer is technically available but not productive. A switcher that cannot identify the next trailer to move is on the payroll but not adding throughput. A shipment that cannot be scheduled may tie up inventory even while the warehouse has labor ready to load it.
The answer matters because building capacity and recovering capacity are different investments. One expands the physical system; the other improves how the existing system is used. In the right circumstances, the second can deliver faster returns with less capital at risk. It will not eliminate every expansion, but it can prevent companies from mistaking operational friction for a structural shortage.
Food manufacturer Red Gold offers a concrete example. Its distribution operations once depended on large volumes of phone calls and email exchanges to coordinate dock appointments. In peak periods, some carriers could face a wait of two weeks to book a slot. That scheduling delay did not mean the operation had no physical space in an absolute sense; it meant access to available capacity was poorly coordinated.
In a case study published by Opendock and Loadsmart , Red Gold reported moving more than 60,000 annual appointments into online carrier self-scheduling. Appointment lead times fell 90%, from double-digit days to roughly one or two days, and case throughput increased 18%. The customer also introduced transportation management and brokerage changes, including ShipperGuide. It would therefore be too simplistic to credit every improvement to a single scheduling product.
The operational logic is nevertheless compelling. The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI . And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. items.description: Anthropic 发布博客，拆解常驻智能体（always-on agents）背后的架构。这类智能体有状态且可主动行动，其兴起得益于模型判断力提升和智能成本下降，例如长程编码任务上 Opus 5.5 每解决一个任务的成本比 Opus 5 低 78%。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ypeap2t8w4fqqfuvt7mw3wg79
items.excerpt:
Anthropic 发布博客，拆解常驻智能体（always-on agents）背后的架构。这类智能体有状态且可主动行动，其兴起得益于模型判断力提升和智能成本下降，例如长程编码任务上 Opus 5.5 每解决一个任务的成本比 Opus 5 低 78%。
Anthropic 把常驻智能体拆成五个可落地的架构原语，并给出实现细节与最佳实践，读者可按此搭建自己的方案。
常驻智能体是有状态、主动的，也就是说，它们能跨会话管理上下文，并在没有直接监督的情况下采取行动。底层上，它们和其他智能体运行在同一个 核心循环 上。区别在于外围架构：这套架构由若干基础构件组成，用来控制智能体何时唤醒、每次运行之间保留什么，以及它们的工作如何送达用户。
这波回潮很大程度上源于近期的模型进步，让常驻智能体运行起来更实际。首先，最新模型的判断力更强：它们更能可靠地理解用户意图，也知道什么时候该来确认一下。其次，智能成本在下降，长周期任务受益最大。例如，在 一个长周期编程基准 上，Opus 5.5 每解决一个任务的花费比 Opus 5 低 78%，而典型工作负载下只低 40%。
客户开始问我们，如何把这种体验集成到自己的产品里。有些公司想让现有智能体更主动，另一些则打算从头构建。
实际上，智能体大部分时间都在休眠，定期醒来干活。每一段工作称为一次 运行 （run）：智能体收到一个事件，完成任务，然后保存发生了什么。运行在 会话 （session）中进行，会话是消息和工具调用的记录。运行结束后，智能体重新休眠，这个循环无限重复。
常驻智能体的外围架构有五个核心基础构件：事件收件箱、定时器、记忆、权限和发件箱。下面逐一来看。
大多数 AI 智能体只在用户发消息时运行。相比之下，常驻智能体可以由多种事件触发，包括 webhook、定时任务和后台作业。
一种诱人的做法是让每个事件源直接调用智能体，但这有几种失败模式。例如，两个事件同时到达，可能启动相互竞争的运行；一次崩溃则可能彻底丢失一个事件。
这就是事件收件箱的用武之地。每个来源不直接调用智能体，而是把事件发送到收件箱，由工作进程取走处理。
收件箱应跟踪每个事件的状态，并可根据来源提供的唯一标识符对事件去重。关系型数据库很适合做收件箱，每个事件作为新行追加。我们建议先从每个用户一个收件箱开始，如果需要更高并行度，可以进一步拆分。
新事件到来时，处理器把事件写入收件箱并唤醒工作进程。工作进程读取所有待处理事件，启动一次运行。延续先前工作的事件（例如用户的回复）会恢复现有会话，其他事件则开启新会话。
随后，worker 把事件交给智能体循环，等待本次运行结束，再把对应事件标记为已完成。具体实现有不少门道，下面列出几条最佳实践：
定时器与事件收件箱配合，让常驻智能体具备主动性。定时器一般分两类：跟进和日程。跟进是智能体给自己设的截止时间，比如到点去查看某个回复；日程则是按固定节奏重复执行的任务，比如每日简报。
定时器存放在自己独立的持久化存储里，通常是另一张数据库表，与收件箱分开。收件箱只应存放已经可以处理的事件。跟进和日程可以共用相似的 schema，但日程还需要额外记录重复规则。
定时器本身不会发起运行。真正干活的是调度器，通常是一个后台服务，它按固定间隔轮询存储，把到期的定时器触发出去。每一轮调度中，调度器会：
和事件收件箱、定时器一样，记忆也应有自己的存储。在我们的产品里，比如 Claude Code 的 auto memory 和 Messages API 的 memory tool ，记忆被实现为一个文件目录。对常驻智能体来说，这些目录应映射到持久化存储，通常是数据库或对象存储，这样记忆的生命周期就能长于 worker。
一条经验法则是：记忆只应保存智能体无法再次查到的东西。如果某些信息已经存在于其他系统（比如问题跟踪器），那就存一个指针即可。下面是常驻智能体应当保存的记忆类型：
以上说的都是运行期间保存的记忆。你还可以加入“做梦”机制，回顾过去的会话以整理记忆。做梦可以替换过时的条目，并发现只有跨多次运行才会显现的规律。如果想了解更多，我们的 智能体记忆文章 有更详细的介绍。
在开始任何工作之前，智能体会加载系统提示词、工具定义和记忆文件。这部分初始上下文的“开销”会包含在每次运行中，所以我们建议保持精简，并使用 提示词缓存 来降低成本。
新会话开始时只有这部分上下文开销，以及触发本次运行的事件。而已有会话则会带回它此前各次运行中的消息和工具调用。
如果会话变得过长，你可以 压缩较早的消息 ，或者开启一个新会话。这两种做法都会丢失细节，所以任何需要长期保留的内容都应当随时写入记忆。
权限是常驻智能体风险最大的地方。一次运行持有用户的访问权限，而且按设计是在无人值守的情况下运作。对每次工具调用，智能体都需要判断是自己继续执行、阻止，还是等待批准。
大多数 AI 智能体在生成回复时会实时流式输出给用户，让用户能跟随 Claude 一步步推理问题、调用工具并写出答案。
而常驻智能体的大部分工作都在后台完成。用户拿到的是结果和少量细节，而不是完整的逐步过程。
大多数常驻智能体用一个“发送”工具直接把消息送达用户就够了。只有当你需要控制智能体发消息的节奏，或让智能体从错误中恢复时，才需要正式的发件箱。
发件箱是一张单独存放待发消息的表，对应事件收件箱。此外还有一个调度器，通常是后台服务，对应工作进程。调度器读取待发消息，决定投递哪些，再把它们发送给用户。延迟工具调用发出的请求既可以走发件箱，也可以直接在界面中展示。
除了投递，调节智能体发送消息的数量也很重要。发得太多会变得吵闹，发得太少又会漏掉用户需要知道的事情。我们建议通过构建评估来找到合适的平衡点。实践中，智能体最好一开始保持安静，再逐步赢得用户更多的关注。
每次运行都始于收件箱中的一个事件，无论是用户消息、webhook 还是定时器。工作进程取到事件后，就启动一次运行，在新的或已有的会话中唤醒智能体。智能体读取记忆以获得基线，在权限范围内

items.title: Google 展示 Antigravity /teamwork 多智能体协作成果并开放给研究者使用
items.description: Google Research 介绍其团队与学术伙伴用 Antigravity 的 /teamwork 多智能体工作流配合 Gemini 4 Argon、Carbon、Hydrogen 模型，在信息论、形式化验证、分子结构和内核优化等领域取得多项成果。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/h0obmlpmc44dqk1da164ca1z7
items.excerpt:
Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity’s /teamwork
Google Research 介绍其团队与学术伙伴用 Antigravity 的 /teamwork 多智能体工作流配合 Gemini 4 Argon 、Carbon、Hydrogen 模型，在信息论、形式化验证、分子结构和内核优化等领域取得多项成果。
原文展示了 /teamwork 多智能体工作流在数学证明、形式化验证和系统优化中的具体成果，读者可据此评估其在自己研究或工程中的适用性。
过去几周，Google 各团队与学术合作机构一起，攻克了数学、科学和复杂系统工程领域悬而未决多年的开放问题。借助 Gemini 4 Argon 、 Gemini 4 Carbon 、 Gemini 4 Hydrogen ，以及 Antigravity 的 /teamwork 等多智能体工作流（基于多个 Gemini 模型构建），这些合作在信息论、形式化验证、分子结构发现和内核优化等方面带来了新的突破，同时也在 Google 内部取得了多项生产基础设施方面的收益。我们正在 Antigravity 的 /teamwork 中开放这些智能体工具（与 /boost 及其他智能体并列），让研究者和开发者能将其用于自己的工作。
前沿研究和系统工程需要梳理海量文献、搭建定制计算流水线、对照物理测量结果进行测试，并逐步验证每一个环节。进展来自一个交互式的发现循环：研究者提出问题、定义理论或物理约束，而长时程智能体负责编写定制求解器、探索庞大的搜索空间、测试候选设计，并检查长长的逻辑链条。
当前语言模型的两大局限，正是 /teamwork 的设计出发点 。其一，模型生成具有不确定性，单次尝试与找到正确答案之间往往存在差距。系统通过并行探索配合专门的证伪器来弥合这一差距，例如 Lean 4 证明检查器、未经修改的软件测试套件、执行模拟器、网络搜索或硬件计数器，自动验证哪些候选方案真正可行。
其二，在多天的任务中，AI 模型常常会丢失细节，因为注意力会随着上下文窗口不断增长而分散。 /teamwork 从结构上对上下文进行分区来避免这一问题：每个专用智能体只拿到特定步骤所需的文件和工具。协调者把任务交给全新的后继智能体，而评审者和审计者则在干净的上下文中质疑并验证结果，不接触原始产出者的推理过程。
Teamwork 将这些工作流表达为声明式、可自我改进的自然语言模式，并把每条用户提示词动态路由到最适合该任务的模式。这些模式涵盖分布式编码和迭代式问题求解（作为 /boost 独立打包，这是一个从既往轨迹中提炼出的顺序求解—验证循环），也涵盖长证明、文档审阅等专门的研究工作流，目前均已在 Antigravity 中提供。团队因此可以基于过往运行记录设计自定义规范，在不同执行框架模式之间路由，并动态改进智能体执行框架。这些功能大多已在 Antigravity 中可用，未来几周我们还会带来更多更新，向 Antigravity 的外部用户提供全部功能。继 此前关于 Antigravity /teamwork 的文章 之后，我们在此公布由 /teamwork 新变体和 Gemini 4 模型赋能、针对开放挑战取得的新成果。
在数学与理论计算机科学领域，研究人员借助 Gemini 4 和 /teamwork 工具链协作完成大规模证明，并能直接从开放问题陈述出发，生成完整的算法与证明。我们在此展示几个例子。
来自 Google、 CUHK 、 USC 和 CMU 的研究人员使用 /teamwork 的 长证明模式 （在 Antigravity 中实现 Stellar Colosseum ），在完全一般的情形下 证明 了信息论中的 2013 年 Courtade–Kumar 猜想 。该结果确认：当随机比特串通过有噪信道时，把输入压缩成单个比特的任何做法，所保留的信息都不如“独裁函数”——它只是复制单个输入比特。Gemini 首先找到了 CUHK 团队 早先论文 中一个推广猜想的反例。随后 CUHK 团队提出了一个新的候选函数，把该猜想归结为一个 14 变量优化问题，并给出了一个关键的分析下界。接着，Gemini 4 Argon 和更早的 Gemini 模型划分了参数空间，推导出大部分新的分析界和区间算术证书。它们还在没有人工输入的情况下，把证明从平衡函数推广到了非平衡函数。团队在 Lean 4 中形式化了整个证明，生成了 5000 万行代码。
研究人员还直接把开放问题交给 Gemini 4 以及 Stellar Colosseum、 /teamwork 等多智能体工具链，得到了端到端的算法与证明（通常附带 Lean 4 形式化），并由作者验证、简化和编辑后发表。在自适应数据分析中，运行于 Gemini 4 Argon 的多智能体工具链独立证明并经 Lean 验证了 近最优样本界 ，适用于根据先前答案自适应选择的统计查询，填补了自 2014 年以来悬而未决的空白。这些界给出了首个 近乎空间最优的算法 ，可用于同时包含插入和删除的数据流，并且面对自适应对手时仍保持准确。在量子计算中，一项新构造 解决了一个 2014 年的开放问题 ：它找到了首批在常数误差下需要严格多于 n /2 次量子查询的 n 比特布尔函数，同时精确确定了对称函数上的查询开销。
多项成果打破了处理与压缩大型矩阵和图结构长期存在的壁垒。在 STOC 2024 之前的五十年里，针对 布尔矩阵乘法与三角形检测 的组合算法（避开快速矩阵乘法中的代数消去）相比立方时间只节省了对数因子。一项新的确定性算法解决了 STOC 2024 的主要未解问题，实现了其相对于立方时间的目标加速。在高维几何中，一项 新的下界 解决了一个关于稀疏网络的 未解问题 ，证明在任意常数因子内近似 n 个点之间的所有两两距离，可能需要多项式级多于 n 条边，即使允许额外的 Steiner 点 和任意多跳。在随机线

items.excerpt:
Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family.
It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme:
Carbon and Argon are the same price , and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task.
Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.50, so Hydrogen is 15x that.
I had Hydrogen generate some pelicans . Here's a full comparison grid showing the pelicans for all three members of the Gemini 4 family at their three supported effort levels:
Considering how close they are in price, the difference in pelican quality for Hydrogen is quite stark.
Here's how Google describe Hydrogen's intended position in their mix of models:
In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.
Most notably, Hydrogen is the new free tier model, and is the model that will power AI features in Google Search.

items.title: 民主党对 Nvidia 对华芯片销售启动调查，致函质疑黄仁勋与特朗普的安排
items.description: 民主党议员 Rep. Richard Neal 和 Sen. Ron Wyden 就特朗普政府处理 Nvidia 对华芯片销售一事开启调查，并致函商务部长 Howard Lutnick 要求保存相关记录。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/cfh0nazzl7eedgttz8n99fza4
items.excerpt:
Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
民主党议员 Rep. Richard Neal 和 Sen. Ron Wyden 就特朗普政府处理 Nvidia 对华芯片销售一事开启调查，并致函商务部长 Howard Lutnick 要求保存相关记录。
原文梳理了民主党对 Nvidia 对华芯片销售安排的调查要点，包括关税分成与许可细节，读者可借此了解监管争议的具体脉络。
民主党人周四启动调查，追问特朗普政府如何处理英伟达对华芯片销售。就在周四早些时候，该公司 罢免了CEO黄仁勋 。他还同意向另一组由共和党主导的国会委员会作证。
黄仁勋是在 承认婚外情 后被逐出他创办的公司的，此前有报道称他与一名被指为中国间谍的女子有染。（此后他又被指控与英伟达员工有 更多婚外情 。）
这名被指为中国间谍的女子是Alice Huang，她是英伟达客户Megaspeed的高管。Megaspeed是一家总部位于新加坡的公司，美国官员怀疑它协助将先进的英伟达芯片转运入中国。此次民主党调查由众议院筹款委员会民主党首席议员、马萨诸塞州众议员Richard Neal和参议院财政委员会民主党首席议员、俄勒冈州参议员Ron Wyden发起。作为少数党，他们可以提问，但无权强制对方作答。
他们给商务部长Howard Lutnick写了一封 措辞犀利的信 ，要求该部门保全与一项他们认为可疑、并指控其违法的安排有关的记录。
信中这样描述该方案：特朗普总统同意英伟达向中国销售H200芯片，条件是这些在台湾制造的芯片须先运往美国。信中说，芯片一到美国，特朗普就加征关税，“实际上是通过一套似乎违宪的出口税体系，从英伟达对华销售中抽成”。随后，Lutnick领导的商务部签发了出口许可证。
顺便一提，特朗普与英伟达之间的收入分成协议是公开的。据 美联社当时报道 ，2025年8月，英伟达和AMD都同意将与对华芯片销售相关的收入的15%分给美国政府，作为换取出口许可协议的一部分。
但信中质疑：据报道Lutnick已从美国情报部门获悉对Alice Huang的怀疑以及黄仁勋与她关系的相关信息，为何仍继续允许Megaspeed购买芯片？信中还质问，为何据报道商务部又批准其他亚洲公司购买英伟达芯片，而这些公司“在其登记地址并无实体存在”。可见这项调查针对的是政府，而不只是英伟达和黄仁勋。
信中还质疑英伟达对特朗普项目的捐款在其中起了什么作用。信中指出，这项出口协议是在特朗普得知“黄先生因与一名疑似间谍上床而处于易受要挟的境地”之后、以及英伟达向特朗普的项目（包括宴会厅）捐款2600万美元之后才获批的。这似乎是在问，特朗普是否利用自己对这段婚外情的了解来换取英伟达的捐款。
有意思的是，在周日播出的特朗普总统接受“60分钟”采访时，他提到自己和团队 曾威胁要把一名未具名的AI高管送进监狱 ，此后这名高管“彻底变了”。

items.title: Super Intelligence-Era Critical Infrastructure Cyber Defense Plan
items.description: A Public-Private Partnership to Defend America’s Critical Infrastructure
items.excerpt:
A16Z’s Anne Neuberger, General Partner and Head of Global Affairs, writes today in the Wall Street Journal:
AI is shrinking the time between when a weakness is found and when it is exploited. Defenders who still work at human speed will lose that race.
The same AI can work for defenders: finding exposed systems, ranking which matter most and generating fixes. For old equipment that can’t be patched, AI can create workarounds, such as a firewall rule or a settings change. The question is whether it can be applied fast enough.
The most significant national risk is concentrated, fortunately. Failures that would cascade across the country run through a few hundred operators and their shared vendors: large transmission substations, the Fedwire and ACH payment systems, water utilities serving big cities, core telecom networks and 911 systems, regional trauma centers and the health-record vendors. Smaller operators matter too, often as soft entry points, but protecting the critical few first buys time to fix the rest.
Drawing on her experience as Deputy National Security Advisor for Cyber and Emerging Threats for the United States, Anne outlines a plan for a new model to drive national cyber resilience, accountable to the White House’s Super Intelligence Force, and led by CEOs of key American companies responsible for critical infrastructure:
The U.S. must address the significant risk that a cyber attack disrupts the operation of critical infrastructure that a large number of Americans rely on. This cyber defense plan outlines the governance and actions that are necessary to identify and contain the exposure at the few hundred operators and shared vendors whose failure would cascade nationally. The plan of action aims to (a) put in place adequate cybersecurity in each sector, accounting for many old, unmanaged systems, (b) use SI to find and fix vulnerabilities in sector-specific, broadly used code, and (c) create AI guides or harnesses for organizations’ unaddressed vulnerabilities to allow for rapid ID’ing of necessary patches as new models come out. A second phase of this work would establish digital replicas or “twins” of critical, shared systems across sectors to enable regular testing of shared systems.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.excerpt:
LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.
To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.
Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview . We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.
JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.

items.description: An automated warehouse can look flawless in a vendor demonstration. Pallets move along a defined route, robots complete carefully sequenced tasks, and the control software displays a continuous flow of work. Then an actual shipment arrives with an uneven pallet, a damaged label, or a load profile that falls outside the assumptions used in the […] The post Why Warehouse Automation ROI Can Fail Before the Robot Starts Working appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
An automated warehouse can look flawless in a vendor demonstration. Pallets move along a defined route, robots complete carefully sequenced tasks, and the control software displays a continuous flow of work. Then an actual shipment arrives with an uneven pallet, a damaged label, or a load profile that falls outside the assumptions used in the design. The robot may be working exactly as intended. The operation still slows down.
That is the uncomfortable truth in many automation business cases: a machine’s rated capacity is not the same thing as a distribution center’s realized capacity. The difference is created by everything the machine depends on—product presentation, packaging, pallet quality, data accuracy, software integration , human exception management, and the ability of the next process to accept what the machine produces. Those dependencies are neither exciting nor photogenic. They can, however, decide whether a multimillion-dollar investment earns its return.
Examples involving XPO Logistics, Staples, and Del Papa Distributing illustrate the issue from different directions. They are examples of organizations addressing the surrounding operating system, not evidence that their automation investments failed. Their experience deserves attention precisely because the mechanical equipment is only part of the story.
At XPO Logistics’ fresh-goods operation in Nieuwegein, Netherlands, incoming products move into an automated crane warehouse. Before they enter the system, pallets undergo inspection. When the criteria for rejection do not match the actual requirements of the equipment, pallets can be diverted, placed on support pallets, or reloaded, consuming labor and slowing an operation designed to minimize manual handling.

items.description: SemiAnalysis 长文分析黄仁勋辞任 Nvidia CEO 后的连锁影响，作者推测其去职与 GPU 走私及美国推动 RASA 出口管制立法有关。文中指出公司约 60 名直管高管的扁平结构依赖黄本人，继任者 Colette Kress 为临时 CEO，Ian Buck 与 Jonah Alben 被视为技术侧人选但无人能全面接替。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/n73ab4h9gqlu6ucv69ynzxln4
items.excerpt:
SemiAnalysis 长文分析黄仁勋辞任 Nvidia CEO 后的连锁影响，作者推测其去职与 GPU 走私及美国推动 RASA 出口管制立法有关。文中指出公司约 60 名直管高管的扁平结构依赖黄本人，继任者 Colette Kress 为临时 CEO，Ian Buck 与 Jonah Alben 被视为技术侧人选但无人能全面接替。
SemiAnalysis 分析黄仁勋辞任后的 Nvidia 继任困境、供应链锁定松动与中国 GPU 走私案，并讨论 RASA 法案可能带来的出口管制影响。
黄仁勋已不再担任英伟达CEO 。英伟达董事会此前正在调查黄仁勋的行为，并权衡他在自己创办的公司的未来，而显然这个行为问题确实存在；与一名身为中国共产党资产的客户以及多名下属保持关系，在道德上是有问题的。
此外，我们认为他仅仅四天后就辞职，背后还有更多因素。我们相信这与大规模GPU走私直接相关。我们的 加速器模型 追踪每一块AI芯片的产量和去向， 我们的数据显示，超过1.5GW 的受限英伟达芯片最终仍然流入了中国。这个数字甚至还不包括 英伟达为规避美国规定而专门制造的芯片，这个故事最初是我们率先报道的 。
我们认为，美国情报界在推动黄仁勋离开英伟达这件事上起了很大作用。具体来说，我们认为很可能RASA或类似立法——该法案已在众议院通过——将会继续推进。随着黄仁勋这位最大的捍卫者离去，对中国的AI和芯片限制现在会以快得多的速度加码。我们坚决支持某些限制，但设计糟糕的限制会损害美国利益。
以下是当前这种格局的明显好处——中国实验室能够远程访问GPU，而 不是 在中国境内：
英伟达、AMD、博通、谷歌、亚马逊、微软、Meta、超微和戴尔等美国公司，其供应链都依赖中国公司。
英伟达和AMD等美国公司雇用中国工程师（明确一下，是居住在中国的工程师）为其GPU系统开发硬件和底层软件。没有这些工程师，我们确信这些GPU的用户体验会明显不如今天。
美国公司，尤其是整个初创企业生态，都受益于中国公司、学生和独立研究人员今天使用这些GPU所发表的开源研究。
来自中国的创新通过广泛专家并行、开源内核库MSA、DeepEP、DeepGEMM等开放创新流向全球。
话虽如此，我们确实支持对中国实施某些AI限制，但这些限制更应该像MATCH法案，而不是RASA。拜登式的扩散规则最有道理。
也许最重要的是： 开源正受到攻击 。英伟达直接与中国实验室在开源方面合作，帮助他们优化GPU和模型，这已是公开的秘密。这些实验室使用Blackwell GPU，英伟达对此心知肚明。美国的开源生态和许多初创企业依赖中国的AI模型。随着黄仁勋离去、对华鹰派获胜，这一点将受到严重损害。
但对股东（以及AI供应链）来说，真正重要的问题是另一个：没有黄仁勋的英伟达是什么？
我们的看法是，这家公司从来就不是为“没有他”而建的。他掌舵33年，即便董事会施压让他离开（或者说是他“辞职”），英伟达有他在，处境仍会明显好过没有他。这家公司是独一无二地按照这个人量身打造的。没有这个人，公司可能会是完全不同的另一头巨兽。SpaceX和特斯拉离了马斯克转不动，英伟达离了黄仁勋也转不动。
对英伟达这样规模和体量的公司来说，它的公司结构相当奇怪。根据黄仁勋的公开说法，他大约有60个直接下属。他说过，CEO就应该有最多的直接下属，因为这些人需要的管理最少，而且他不跟他们开一对一会议。
但他们中很少有人能在没有黄仁勋的情况下做事。公司就像一个王国，只有一个国王，其他所有人无论资历多高，都是听他差遣的小卒。黄仁勋说过，谁向谁汇报并不重要，因为头衔与工作的重要性无关，这也是英伟达是“世界上最小的大公司”、员工人数少得多——约4.2万人——却拥有巨大市值的原因之一。正因如此，英伟达内部的办公室政治更少。黄仁勋说，这种扁平网络赋予员工权力，让公司能更快适应变化，因为它的技术也在飞速演进。
这是英伟达跑得快的原因之一。一旦黄仁勋定下方向，所有人就一起朝那个方向行动。前员工告诉我们，产品开发和工程常常做到最后一刻，这样公司需要时还能改主意。例如，一位前高管告诉我们，GB200的设计定稿时间比大概任何人希望的都更贴近产品周期。黄仁勋说过，他希望自己能永远让公司保持创业状态。
然而这种结构的代价是，英伟达没有深厚的接班人选储备。看看英伟达的网站：在他的汇报对象中，只有另外五人被重点展示，其中两人是法务和财务高管。他的大多数直接下属都没有接受过面对聚光灯的训练，还被明确劝阻去追求曝光。很少有人离职去别的巨头当CEO，Arm的雷内·哈斯是罕见的例外。在英伟达，很少有人有机会在外部发光，因为所有重大决定都由黄仁勋来做。但英伟达高管团队的很多人并不介意，因为欲戴王冠必承其重，而且许多人乐意干到退休年龄，因为薪酬优厚、待遇好，也相信公司的使命和他们的领袖。
科莱特·克雷斯已被任命为临时CEO，但英伟达正在寻找一位正式CEO。这个人不能有财务背景。技术方面被外界提及、有望接替黄仁勋的明显内部人选是伊恩·巴克和乔纳·阿尔本。巴克在斯坦福读博期间的研究催生了CUDA，2004年加入英伟达，如今作为超大规模和高性能计算副总裁负责数据中心业务。黄仁勋出差时，经常由他负责事务，他也经常在会议上发言。
阿尔本 1997 年就加入英伟达，现任 GPU 工程高级副总裁，负责公司 GPU 的设计。但现实地说，没有哪一个人能统管全部。我们认为巴克没有能力掌管技术硬件工程这一块。阿尔本及其团队中的其他人拥有技术自主权，但即便是他，也无法掌控整个芯片业务，那里还有其他高级负责人掌管着许多重要的技术和业务部门，他们也直接向黄仁勋汇报。两人都很出色，但恐怕都不具备黄仁勋那样的供应链掌控力。

Robots will enter trials in warehouse workflows including goods-to-person and person-to-goods picking, case and tote movement, packing, and sortation.
Contract logistics provider GXO will expand its deployment of humanoid robots from Apptronik in a deal that could reach a global rollout of up to 1,000 humanoid robots over the next four years.
The initial deployment of those robots in North America would start in late 2027, according to a letter of intent (LOI) between the two companies.
GXO and Apptronik will expand joint trials of Apptronik’s “Apollo” model robot in live operations across a range of warehouse workflows, including goods-to-person and person-to-goods picking, case and tote movement, packing, and sortation. Beginning in 2027, the trials will validate the safety, security and technical requirements for scaled deployment – with each use case assessed and sequenced against jointly agreed productivity, safety and operational KPIs – and demonstrate how humanoids can work alongside existing automation and GXO team members.
Subject to the success of the deployments and the ability to meet agreed performance, safety, and operational KPIs, the companies intend to progress toward global rollout of up to 1,000 Apollo humanoid robots over the next four years, under a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.
“We started working with GXO in 2024, and through our partnership we’re defining what it takes to put humanoid robots to work in logistics — measured against real operational KPIs in live facilities, and delivering real value,” said Jeff Cardenas, CEO and co-founder of Apptronik. “GXO has the network and the operating discipline to take this technology to real scale, across one of the largest logistics footprints in the world.”
GXO launched a proof-of-concept test in 2024 of Austin, Texas-based Apptronik’s robots, with a goal of finding practical applications in a warehouse environment. It then expanded that deal in 2026 from an initial application in a Georgia DC to additional warehouses in North Carolina and Tennessee.

items.excerpt:
IFR report finds that global manufacturing sector has reached a new peak, led by South Korea, Singapore, and Germany.
Robot density in the global manufacturing sector has reached a new peak, led by South Korea, Singapore, and Germany, according to the International Federation of Robotics (IFR).
South Korea remains the world’s undisputed leader in robot density, with 1,066 industrial units per 10,000 employees. Singapore follows in second place with 873 units, while Germany secures third place, at 469 units. All three nations vastly outperformed the new global average baseline, which has risen to 152 units per 10,000 employees.
In other regions, robot density in the European Union (EU-27) increased by around 35 % within five years (2020-2025), reaching a new record of 240 units. Five of the top ten most automated economies are members of the European Union: Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Slovenia and the Netherlands. North America´s robot density rose by around 24 % over the same period (2020-2025) reaching 214 units. The United States remain 8th worldwide with 323 units per 10,000 employees. Canada follows with 242 units and Mexico with 64 units. Robot density in Asia increased by about 47 % within five years (2020-2025), reaching 144 units. Next to the region's front runners, South Korea and Singapore, Japan with 452 units ranks in 4th position among the top 10 most automated manufacturing countries. China, as the world´s largest market for industrial robots, now has a robot density of 193 units per 10,000 employees – ranking 19th globally. This result is based on employment data of the National Economic Census, conducted by China's National Bureau of Statistics. China’s robot density increased by 147 % from 2020 through 2025.

items.excerpt:
Move comes amid challenges such as trade-policy shifts, economic uncertainty, and supply disruptions.
Manufacturers in North American are strengthening factory resilience by restructuring regional production and supply networks to sustain production amid challenges such as trade-policy shifts, economic uncertainty, and supply disruptions, according to a report from Information Services Group (ISG).
In a bid to preserve safety, continuity, and traceability, manufacturers are coordinating product, plant, and service workflows, the tech research firm said in its “2026 ISG Provider Lens Manufacturing Industry Services and Solutions” report.
Aging plants and regional supplier networks make this coordination especially important. Companies are pursuing AI deployment and brownfield modernization while addressing the need for workforce skills and local support.
“North American manufacturers are making operational continuity a central requirement for technology decisions,” said Bob Krohn, ISG partner, manufacturing. “Technology must fit the realities of aging assets, skill shortages and live production environments.”
At plants, enterprises are incorporating manufacturing execution systems, quality systems, maintenance, and SCADA data into a common production context. They are evaluating physical AI for machine vision, adaptive process control, autonomous material movement, and predictive maintenance. These applications require simulation, human oversight, safety assurance, and rollback-tested deployment before influencing physical operations.
Companies are also upgrading smart-factory capabilities in brownfield environments while limiting downtime and cyber exposure. Supply chain control towers are incorporating supplier, inventory, transport, and plant constraints for stronger regional traceability. Aftermarket programs combine connected-asset data, spare-parts planning, field service, and reverse logistics to support service lifecycles.
The report also explores other trends affecting North American manufacturers, including the rising need for workforce enablement for technicians and operators and industrial cybersecurity for control systems.

items.excerpt:
To hear more from Elena Burger , Anish A , and Jon Lai on this topic, check out the companion podcast to this piece here .
If you want to understand an industry, study its favorite archetypes.
In the case of gaming, first there’s the indie dev. This category includes guys like Eric Barone (the creator of Stardew Valley ), Jonathan Blow ( Braid , The Witness , and Order of the Sinking Star ), and small teams like Tarn and Zach Adams (co-creators of the epic, sprawling world-sim Dwarf Fortress ). People like these developers and the games they create because despite all odds they were able to create a commercial success well outside of the warm confines of a conventional studio. They are the gaming equivalent of the nerdy guy getting the girl. The fact that these games could succeed at all is part of their appeal (they are also, of course, quite fun).
Then there is the prophetic toolmaker: guys like Tim Sweeney and John Carmack. These are people whose experiments programming bare-metal and pushing the boundaries of hardware later expanded what other people could build. Their work produced engines, editors, and simulations that eventually became environments for other people to build in.
Finally, there is the world-building studio. These are teams like Rockstar Games ( Red Dead Redemption 2 and the upcoming GTA VI ) or Larian Studios ( Baldur’s Gate 3 ) who spend years constructing a place whose detail and verisimilitude (not to mention tiny easter eggs) exceed anything one player is likely to notice. As examples: Red Dead’s wildlife includes possums playing dead and bears bluff-charging and GTA VI will have six in-game radio stations (including one hosted by fictional characters voiced by Lana Del Rey and her husband). People love these games because of how lived-in they feel.
These archetypes gesture at different values: indie devs get to toil away at their specific vision, and occasionally strike gold when that vision resonates. The prophetic toolmakers are responsible for pushing a technical boundary. And the world-building studios construct a game of extraordinary depth.

Praxis-1 builds on Runway’s work as a founding member of the Cosmos Coalition, advancing open world models for physical AI. | Source: Runway
Runway AI Inc. yesterday released Praxis-1, its world action model for robotics. The model is now available to developers with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license.
Runway first announced Praxis-1 in September with launch partners including Noble Machines , Standard Bots , and Ultra . Since then, these companies have been running the model on their own hardware, including a legged humanoid , a six-axis industrial arm, and a dual-arm warehouse robot.
“A strong base model goes a long way. Earlier, with Noble Machines, our previous model needed a lot of training to learn their warehouse task: picking up wooden planks one at a time and placing them in a container,” Andy Chen, the head of robotics at Runway, told The Robot Report . “Praxis-1, built with more compute and data, learned it from half an hour of examples and got it right 15 times out of 15. Then we gave it a messy pile of planks it had never seen to clear into bins, and it cleared the whole pile six times out of 10.”
“Iterating on feedback from partners makes our models better,” he continued. “Today, Praxis-1 is the top-ranked world action model on NVIDIA’s RoboLab leaderboard , and the top-ranked open-source, end-to-end policy.”
Praxis-1 is available on GitHub , on Hugging Face with native LeRobot support , and in vLLM-Omni, with hosted inference on Reactor . Runway said it released everything developers need to run and adapt the model on their own hardware under Apache 2.0, including for commercial use. That covers the weights and the inference and fine-tuning code, with support for both full fine-tuning and low-rank adaptation ( LoRA ).
Praxis-1 runs out of the box across NVIDIA hardware, from data center GPUs such as the H100 and B200, to workstation GPUs like the RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000, to Jetson Thor on the robot itself.
Praxis-1 is a 27B-parameter mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer that predicts video and actions together.

items.excerpt:
A truck delivers fresh produce to a supermarket and heads toward its next assignment. The produce has been received, but the logistics transaction is not complete. There are empty crates in the store that belong somewhere else, must be cleaned before being reused, and need to return to circulation before the next shipping cycle. In a disposable packaging model, much of that work ended with a recycling or waste stream. In a reusable model, it becomes an operating obligation with its own assets, service levels, and economics.
Reusable pallets, crates, and consumer containers are commonly discussed in environmental terms. That is understandable, given the potential to avoid single-use material. But for logistics executives, a more interesting development is taking place: the return trip itself is becoming a product. Someone must forecast the containers, retrieve them, inspect or sanitize them, reposition them, and have the right quantity available at the next point of use. A reusable package is not an environmental benefit simply because it was designed to be reused. It has to come back, in usable condition, often enough to justify the system around it.
In November 2026, IFCO described an expansion of its program with Whole Foods Market . The initiative began in 2022, initially replacing disposable corrugated cartons for products such as root vegetables with reusable plastic containers. IFCO said the collaboration had avoided nearly four million pounds of cardboard waste since inception and that use of the containers had increased substantially over the period.
Those are supplier-reported environmental and scale figures, but they point to a practical network-design question. A crate arriving with produce must eventually be separated from the merchandise, consolidated, collected, inspected, cleaned, and released for another trip. It also has to arrive back in circulation in the right geography and at the right time. A container sitting in a stockroom is an unavailable transportation asset, even if it has not physically left the supply chain.
This is why a returnable-packaging program cannot be managed solely as a procurement substitution—plastic instead of cardboard, one unit price instead of another. Store operations, food safety, transportation planning, distribution, and the pooling provider all influence whether the loop works. At AI Engineer Code Summit, lead Jev creator Diogo Almeida called on developers to automate everything. Also, Glean and others showed how they’re using Jev.
Today at the AI Engineer Code Summit , the main theme was system one models — non-generative models that return structured choices, scores, or probabilities. They’re also typically much faster and cheaper than reasoning LLMs (a.k.a. system two models).
And who better to give an inspirational rallying cry for system one models than Diogo Almeida , co-founder and CEO of TypeSafe AI . Almeida was lead creator of Jev , the product that kicked off this trend less than two months ago.
Jev was an instant revelation for AI engineers when it was released in September. In a podcast with Latent Space on launch (which quickly became our most popular episode of the year), Almeida explained the core problem with making LLMs the heart of software: reliability .
In his keynote at AIE Code today, he took it a step further by claiming that Jev is “reliable intelligence” that should be used for “just automating everything.”
Of particular interest to AI engineers is Almeida’s point that system one models should become integrated with code. As he put it in his keynote, “code is the language of automation , therefore you need to integrate with code.”
Latent Space founder swyx interprets this as a call to “liberally sprinkle ‘System One’ model calls everywhere INSIDE application code to make smarter software instead of increasingly convoluted forms of ‘concat strings together and hope for the best" AI engineering.’”
The term “smart software” was used throughout Almeida’s presentation. It sounds like the kind of term used by companies like Microsoft or IBM during Web 2.0, but in the AI era it does actually signify a harsh reality about LLM-driven software: sometimes it’s just not very smart. As Almeida quipped during his presentation, “you get Einstein 95% of the time, but Mr. Bean 5% of the time.”
“And if you can't tell which is which, how the fuck are you going to automate anything,” he added.
Almeida ended with an impassioned plea to “automate everything.” Like an AI-pilled, pink-haired Steve Jobs, he called out to “the dreamers and the people who don't want to be limited by everything that has happened so far,” promising that TypeSafe AI wants to “really fight for you, and we want this to be as reliable as a fourth logic gate. ”

items.title: The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models
items.excerpt:
TLDR; In this blog, we provide fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D model on your 3D assets, that can run both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs. If you are interested in fine-tuning, you can use our scripts with few arguments (assuming you updated your dataset to Hugging Face Hub) or tinker with them yourself with this repository . If you want to learn more, we go through how the script works . Let’s go!
3D generation has many uses in robotics, simulation, media, and entertainment. In these fields, it is difficult to make generated objects obey strict rules and standardize model and data representations. There are many file formats, such as GLB and PLY . There are also many representations , such as neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) . Each one has different advantages and disadvantages.
TRELLIS introduced a common internal representation, called a unified latent representation. Its decoders convert this representation into 3D models in the required output format. Thus, you do not have to use different models for each representation format.
The same team then released TRELLIS.2 , which improves the model's representation of 3D structure. But neither model gives an easy way to adapt it to a specific task.

FMC³ Robotics has introduced its Doceo series, a collection of data acquisition and processing technologies designed to help industrial robots learn manufacturing tasks from real-world human activity.
The Germany-based industrial embodied AI company says the system is intended to address one of the main challenges facing intelligent robotics: obtaining sufficiently detailed physical-world data to train robots for tasks that involve complex movements, object handling and changing production conditions.
Rather than relying entirely on dedicated robot training facilities or simulated environments, FMC³ aims to collect data directly from factory operations while workers carry out their normal duties.
The resulting information can then be used to train, test and refine robot capabilities through the company’s Industrial Embodied AI Agent Platform.
The Doceo series consists of four interconnected technologies covering data collection, processing, training infrastructure and robot integration.
Doceo RealCap uses smart camera headsets, external cameras and optional touch-sensitive gloves to capture visual, depth, movement and tactile information as workers perform industrial tasks.
Doceo Hub synchronizes these data streams, combines multiple perspectives and provides tools for recording, playback, annotation and data management.
Doceo Cloud is designed to support data ingestion, automatic labeling, curation, model training, simulation and testing. The system draws on data infrastructure and cloud technologies from Vector Informatik.
Doceo Driver connects the resulting robot capabilities to different robotic platforms and control systems.
Together, the components form what FMC³ describes as an industrial learning loop, connecting real-world task demonstrations with AI model development, validation and subsequent robot operations.
Dr. Joachim Fetzer, president of Europe at FMC³ Robotics, says: “The real shortage is not data in general. It is qualified physical-world data that reflect how a task is actually performed in a certain environment: the movement, physical interactions, process sequence, quality outcomes, and also the errors and corrections.”
FMC³ is also advancing two industrial proof-of-concept projects intended to evaluate its approach under manufacturing conditions.
